name: Allam-Fetvedt cycle (oxy-combustion supercritical CO2 power)
applications: natural gas power with inherent capture

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Natural gas burns in oxygen diluted with hot recycled CO2. The high-pressure CO2 and water mixture drives a turbine, is cooled in a recuperator, and the water is condensed out. Most CO2 is recompressed and recycled; the excess is near-pure and goes straight to a pipeline.

name: Amine solvent post-combustion capture

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Flue gas is cooled and contacted counter-currently with an aqueous amine solution, which reacts with CO2. The CO2-rich solution is heated with low-pressure steam in a stripper, releasing a near-pure CO2 stream and regenerating the solvent for reuse. Vendors differ mainly in solvent formulation, heat integration and solvent management.

name: Bioenergy with CCS (BECCS)
aliases: bioenergy with carbon capture and storage
principle: CO2 from biomass combustion or fermentation is captured and stored, so net emissions are negative. IEA rates bioenergy with post-combustion capture at TRL 7.

name: Calcium looping
applications: cement (purge CaO usable as raw meal)

source.note: Energy & Fuels 38(15), 2024, CC BY 4.0: pilot at TRL7; IEAGHG 2019 gave TRL 6

principle: Lime (CaO) captures CO2 from flue gas in a carbonator at about 650 °C, forming CaCO3. The solids circulate to a calciner at about 900-950 °C, fired with fuel in oxygen and CO2, which releases a concentrated CO2 stream and regenerates CaO. Fresh limestone is added to make up for sorbent decay.

process_steps.name: Heat recovery, CO2 purification and compression

key_equipment: two interconnected circulating fluidised bed reactors

reference_plants.name: La Pereda pilot
reference_plants.capacity: 1.7 MWth
reference_plants.status: biomass-fired calciner tests reached capture efficiencies above 99% in some periods (2024)

source.note: Energy & Fuels 2024, DOI 10.1021/acs.energyfuels.4c02472

advantages: Cheap, abundant sorbent (limestone)
High-temperature heat can be recovered for power
Synergy with cement: spent CaO is a raw material
limitations: Needs an air separation unit for the calciner
Sorbent activity decays with cycles, so make-up and purge are needed

name: Chemical looping combustion

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: A solid metal oxide oxygen carrier circulates between an air reactor, where it picks up oxygen, and a fuel reactor, where it burns the fuel without contact with air. The fuel reactor exhaust is only CO2 and water, so CO2 is obtained by condensing the water, without an air separation unit.

suppliers.name: Research stage; no commercial licensor identified in the cited sources

advantages: Inherent CO2 separation with no air separation unit
limitations: Oxygen carrier attrition and lifetime
Solids circulation at scale not yet demonstrated commercially

name: Cryogenic carbon capture (desublimation)

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Flue gas is dried and cooled to about -117 °C or colder so that CO2 freezes out (desublimes) and is separated as a solid, then melted and pumped as high-purity liquid CO2. Cold is recovered between the incoming and outgoing streams in multi-stream heat exchangers.

name: Electro-swing and moisture-swing DAC

name: Physical solvent acid gas removal (pre-combustion)
principle: At high pressure and high CO2 partial pressure, organic solvents such as chilled methanol (Rectisol) or Selexol dissolve CO2 and H2S without chemical reaction. The rich solvent is depressurised in stages to release CO2, then stripped, and returned to the absorber. Physical solvents favour high-pressure syngas, while chemical solvents suit low partial pressures.

process_steps.name: Acid gas absorption at low temperature

suppliers.name: Rectisol and Selexol licensors (see NETL Gasifipedia)

advantages: Very deep sulfur removal (Rectisol below 0.1 ppmv H2S plus COS per NETL)
Low regeneration heat, since much CO2 is released by pressure let-down
limitations: Needs high pressure and high CO2 partial pressure
Refrigeration makes capital cost two to three times that of chemical solvents (NETL)

principle: Flue gas passes over a CO2-selective polymer membrane. name: Geological CO2 storage in saline aquifers
applications: permanent storage of captured CO2 from industry, power and gas processing
principle: Captured CO2 is compressed to a dense phase, piped or shipped to an injection site and injected through wells into a porous rock formation filled with salt water, below an impermeable caprock. The CO2 is trapped under the seal, dissolves in the brine and, over long periods, can mineralise. Injection raises reservoir pressure, so capacity is limited by the pressure that the rock and caprock can tolerate; operators manage it with well placement, completion design and sometimes brine production. Monitoring wells and surveys track the plume.

performance.metric: storage capacity gain from lateral pressure redistribution by brine production, Natuna D-Alpha (simulation)
performance.basis: thick carbonate aquifer; high-rate brine production; multi-depth injection alone gave 13%, both together 44% with storage efficiency 0.58%

source.note: Nirwana et al., Optimizing CO2 Storage in Saline Aquifers through Pressure Redistribution in Natuna D-Alpha Field, SCOG 49(3): 53-66, 2026 (LEMIGAS SCOG, CC BY-SA 4.0)

performance.metric: increase in stored CO2 from completion redesign, SK gas field aquifer (simulation)
performance.basis: 120-year simulation with plume confined to the aquifer zone in most cases; mineral trapping a minor share

source.note: Iskandar et al., Optimized CO2 storage strategies for plume containment and mineral trapping in the SK gas field aquifer, SCOG 49(2): 173-201, 2026 (LEMIGAS SCOG, CC BY-SA 4.0)

performance.metric: pore pressure rise and remaining margin to fracture pressure, sandstone at 1,200 m (simulation)
performance.basis: pore pressure 11.8 to 15.8 MPa against 19.0 MPa fracture pressure, safety ratio 1.20; 10 years injection plus 500 years monitoring

source.note: Fitria et al., Impact of CO2-Induced Geochemical Alteration on the Mechanical Integrity of Reservoir and Caprock in Saline Aquifers, SCOG 49(3): 607-645, 2026 (LEMIGAS SCOG, CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Amine acid gas removal (MDEA, formulated amines)
principle: Sour gas is contacted with an aqueous amine solution in an absorber, which takes up CO2 and H2S. The rich solution is flashed, heated against lean solution and regenerated by steam stripping, releasing acid gas to a sulfur recovery unit or CO2 handling. MDEA-based formulations can be tuned for selective H2S removal for sales gas or deep CO2 removal for LNG.

process_steps.name: Acid gas disposal
equipment: sulfur recovery unit, CO2 compression for storage, or reinjection

performance.metric: CO2 content of feed gas to LNG pretreatment and after acid gas removal
performance.basis: NETL LNG model: removal from about 7,050 ppmv in pipeline feed to about 50 ppmv (low = outlet, high = inlet)

source.note: NETL, Life Cycle GHG Perspective on Exporting LNG from the United States: 2019 Update, DOE/NETL-2019/2041, 12 September 2019, Exhibits 5-7 and 5-11, Appendix B

name: Boil-off gas management and reliquefaction
principle: Heat leaks into LNG tanks and evaporates a fraction each day. Boil-off gas is used as fuel, burnt in a gas combustion unit or compressed, cooled and returned to the cargo tanks in a reliquefaction plant. Wärtsilä's system compresses boil-off, cools it in a cold box on a nitrogen compression-expansion cycle, removes nitrogen and returns LNG to the tanks.

name: Molecular sieve and glycol dehydration
applications: LNG and NGL cryogenic plants (molecular sieve)
principle: Water is removed so it cannot form hydrates, ice or corrosive liquids. Glycol units absorb water into triethylene glycol, which is regenerated by heating, and are enough for pipeline specifications. Cryogenic plants use molecular sieve beds that adsorb water to very low levels and are regenerated by hot gas in a timed cycle. NETL's LNG model dries gas to below 0.5 ppmv water ahead of liquefaction.

performance.metric: water content after molecular sieve dehydration for LNG
performance.basis: NETL LNG pretreatment assumption (below 0.5 ppmv)

source.note: NETL, Life Cycle GHG Perspective on Exporting LNG from the United States: 2019 Update, DOE/NETL-2019/2041, 12 September 2019, Exhibits 5-7 and 5-11, Appendix B

advantages: Mature and simple
Molecular sieves reach cryogenic dryness
Glycol units are low cost for pipeline gas
limitations: Glycol regeneration vents BTEX and methane unless controlled
Molecular sieves need regeneration heat and periodic replacement
Adsorbent dusting can foul downstream exchangers

sources.note: NETL, Life Cycle GHG Perspective on Exporting LNG from the United States: 2019 Update, DOE/NETL-2019/2041, 12 September 2019, Exhibits 5-7 and 5-11, Appendix B

name: Electric-drive liquefaction (e-LNG)

name: Liquid redox sulfur recovery (LO-CAT)
principle: Hydrogen sulfide is absorbed into an aqueous solution of an iron chelate catalyst, where it is oxidised to elemental sulfur (H2S + 1/2 O2 -> S + H2O). The reduced catalyst is regenerated by air in an oxidiser, and the sulfur is separated as a slurry or cake. The process suits small to mid-size H2S loads and streams that are too lean or too dilute for a Claus plant.

name: Membrane CO2 removal for high-CO2 gas
applications: bulk CO2 removal ahead of amines
principle: Gas flows past a polymer membrane. CO2, H2S and water dissolve into and diffuse through the polymer faster than methane, so they collect on the low-pressure permeate side while methane stays at pressure in the residue. Pretreatment protects the membrane from liquids and heavy hydrocarbons, and two stages or a permeate compressor can be used to reduce methane losses.

name: Mercury removal units
applications: gas processing with aluminium cryogenic exchangers
principle: Gas passes through fixed beds of sorbent, typically metal sulfides on alumina, which react irreversibly with mercury to form stable mercury sulfide. Mercury must be removed because it corrodes aluminium cryogenic heat exchangers. Modern designs place the beds upstream, close to the wells, rather than downstream of dryers as was common historically.

equipment: acid gas removal, dehydration, cryogenic exchangers

Simple fixed beds with no utilities
Upstream placement limits contamination of the whole plant
limitations: Spent sorbent is hazardous waste
Upstream beds must tolerate wet, high-pressure gas
Mercury can also be carried into liquids and needs separate treatment

name: Physical solvent gas treating (Selexol, Rectisol, Purisol)
applications: separate H2S and CO2 streams for sulfur recovery and CO2 storage or EOR
principle: Acid gases dissolve in an organic solvent in proportion to their partial pressure, with no chemical reaction. The rich solvent is released by pressure letdown, flashing and, where H2S must be sent to sulfur recovery, heat or stripping gas, so regeneration needs less heat than amine. Selexol uses dimethyl ethers of polyethylene glycol; Rectisol uses refrigerated methanol. Because capacity rises with pressure, physical solvents suit high-pressure gas such as gasification syngas and not low-pressure gas.

process_steps.name: Feed gas cooling and water removal
Acid gas absorption at high pressure
Staged flash of rich solvent (CO2 release, recycle of co-absorbed hydrocarbons)
Acid gas to sulfur recovery or CO2 handling

name: Ammonia as hydrogen carrier and ammonia cracking

hydrogen supply for power and industry in importing countries such as Japan and Korea

name: Hydrogen storage in salt caverns
applications: buffer between electrolysers and steady users
principle: Caverns are dissolved in deep salt formations by solution mining, then filled with compressed hydrogen. Salt is nearly impermeable to hydrogen and creeps to seal fractures, so caverns can be cycled many times. A cushion gas stays in the cavern to keep the walls stable, and withdrawn gas is dried before use.

name: Steam methane reforming
aliases: Hydrogen production for refining (SMR with PSA)
principle: Natural gas is desulfurised and reacted with steam over a nickel catalyst in externally fired tubes to make syngas. Water-gas shift converts most of the CO to more hydrogen and CO2, and pressure swing adsorption purifies the hydrogen. Without capture the CO2 is vented, partly in the shifted process gas and partly in the reformer flue gas. Blue hydrogen versions capture the process CO2, the flue gas CO2, or both.

name: Solid oxide electrolysis
applications: nuclear or industrial waste-heat coupled hydrogen
principle: A ceramic electrolyte conducts oxide ions at high temperature (650 to 850 °C according to DOE). Part of the energy comes as heat, so electricity use per kilogram is lower than in low-temperature electrolysis, especially when steam comes from process heat.

name: Photocatalytic and thermochemical water splitting
principle: Sunlight splits water directly: photocatalytic and photoelectrochemical devices use photons, while solar thermochemical cycles use concentrated heat (for example a metal-oxide cycle with doped ceria). name: Propane-precooled mixed refrigerant liquefaction (C3MR, AP-X)
principle: A propane refrigeration cycle precools the feed gas and the mixed refrigerant. A mixed refrigerant of nitrogen, methane, ethane and propane then liquefies and subcools the gas in a coil-wound main cryogenic heat exchanger. AP-X adds a nitrogen expander loop that subcools LNG from about -115 °C to about -150 °C, cutting mixed refrigerant flow by 40% per unit of LNG and allowing trains of 7.8 Mtpa and more.

performance.basis: design capacity of the six original Qatar AP-X trains and four North Field East trains; Air Products says trains can exceed 10 Mtpa

source.note: Air Products, LNG technology enables largest LNG trains (printed 2020)

performance.basis: NETL model of a US C3MR plant from Mallapragada et al. 2018; range covers adsorption or cryogenic heavy hydrocarbon removal, with or without HRSG; fuel is a parasitic stream of feed gas, not compressor shaft power

source.note: NETL, Life Cycle GHG Perspective on Exporting LNG from the United States: 2019 Update, DOE/NETL-2019/2041, 12 September 2019, Exhibits 5-7 and 5-11, Appendix B

performance.basis: C3MR configurations (0.347-0.391 kWh/kg); no absolute AP-X value given (one study reports 15.56% lower power than its base case); process simulation of integrated NGL/LNG plants (this study: Aspen Plus, 37 °C air, 25 °C seawater, 3.33 Mtpa); values from different studies on different bases, so compare with care

name: Dual mixed refrigerant liquefaction
principle: Two mixed refrigerant cycles replace the propane-plus-mixed-refrigerant arrangement. A precooling mixed refrigerant cools the gas in spiral-wound precoolers, and a second mixed refrigerant of nitrogen, methane, ethane, propane and some butane liquefies the gas over about -40 °C to -150 °C in the main cryogenic heat exchanger. Adjusting the two compositions lets the plant follow seasonal ambient temperature.

name: Floating storage and regasification units (FSRU)
principle: A ship with LNG tanks and onboard vaporisers is moored at a jetty or buoy. LNG from carriers is transferred ship to ship, stored, pumped to pressure and vaporised with seawater or a closed loop, then sent to shore through a high-pressure arm or pipeline. NETL's import terminal model uses open rack vaporisers, which serve about all Asian and about 60% of European terminals.

equipment: HP gas arm or subsea pipeline

performance.basis: NETL import terminal model (open rack vaporisers)

name: Methanol-to-olefins (MTO, DMTO)
applications: ethylene and propylene from coal- or gas-derived methanol
polyethylene and polypropylene in coal-rich regions
principle: Methanol vapour is converted over a SAPO-34 molecular sieve catalyst in a fluidized-bed reactor into ethylene and propylene. name: Paraxylene adsorption and crystallisation
applications: paraxylene for purified terephthalic acid and polyester
principle: Mixed xylenes from reformate and transalkylation are fed to a simulated-moving-bed adsorption unit. A rotary valve moves feed, desorbent and product ports along beds of selective adsorbent so that, in effect, a counter-current moving bed is created without moving solids; paraxylene is adsorbed and then desorbed, and the desorbent is recovered by distillation. The raffinate is isomerised and recycled to extinction.

name: Propane dehydrogenation (Oleflex, CATOFIN)
applications: propylene for polypropylene where cracker propylene is short
principle: Propane is heated and passed over a dehydrogenation catalyst, which removes hydrogen to form propylene. Ethane gives mostly ethylene; naphtha gives a wider product slate including propylene, butadiene and aromatics.

name: Microreactors (transportable nuclear)

name: Crude and vacuum distillation with heat integration
applications: first separation step in every refinery
principle: Crude is desalted, preheated against hot product streams and heated in a fired furnace, then separated by boiling range in an atmospheric column into gas, naphtha, kerosene, diesel and atmospheric residue. The residue would crack and foul at atmospheric pressure, so it is reheated and split again under vacuum into vacuum gas oils and vacuum residue.

name: Delayed coking and fluid coking
applications: petroleum coke for fuel or anodes
principle: Vacuum residue is heated quickly in a furnace to 480 to 590 °C and sent to a coke drum at about 400 °C and 25 to 30 psig, where it cracks thermally over many hours. Vapours go to a fractionator, and solid coke builds up in the drum. Drums run in pairs on a semi-batch cycle of 28 to 36 hours, with one filling while the other is steamed, cooled and cut out with high-pressure water.

performance.basis: EPA AP-42 description

source.note: US EPA AP-42 Section 5.1 Petroleum Refining (April 2015 revision), process descriptions

Lower pressure and hydrogen demand than resid hydrocracking
limitations: Produces large volumes of coke
Cracked products need severe hydrotreating
Drum cycling and decoking are safety-critical

name: Direct crude cracking
principle: Crude oil, or a light fraction of it, is sent directly to a steam cracker to make olefins and aromatics, skipping some or all of the conventional distillation and conversion steps. ExxonMobil's Singapore cracker started up in 2013 as the first to process crude directly. Saudi Aramco, Lummus and Chevron Lummus Global developed TC2C, which uses steam dilution to vaporise a light cut for the cracker, hydroprocesses a heart cut, and converts the heaviest fraction in liquid-circulation reactors.

name: Fluid catalytic cracking and resid FCC
principle: Hot, fine zeolite catalyst behaves like a fluid and meets vaporised gas oil in a riser reactor at 470 to 525 °C, cracking it into gasoline, LPG, light cycle oil and slurry. Coke deposited on the catalyst is burned off with air in a regenerator at 590 to 675 °C, which reheats the catalyst for the next pass. Residue versions use two-stage regenerators and catalyst coolers.

name: Flare gas recovery and smokeless flares
principle: Elevated flares burn relief and vent gas at the tip of a stack 10 to over 100 m tall, using steam or air assistance for smokeless burning; ground flares burn at ground level, often in enclosures. EPA's AP-42 says properly operated flares achieve at least 98% destruction efficiency, with refinery flares needing at least 270 Btu/ft3 net heating value in the combustion zone. Flare gas recovery compressors return routine flow to fuel gas; see the upstream flare gas recovery card.

name: Visbreaking and solvent deasphalting
principle: Visbreaking mildly thermally cracks vacuum residue to cut its viscosity so less cutter stock is needed for fuel oil. name: Chemical EOR (polymer and surfactant flooding)
applications: extra oil from mature waterflooded fields
principle: Chemicals are added to injection water to recover oil that waterflooding leaves behind. Polymers such as hydrolyzed polyacrylamide (HPAM) raise the viscosity of the injected water so it sweeps the reservoir more evenly and water breaks through later. Surfactants lower the interfacial tension between oil and water so trapped oil droplets can move. Alkali-surfactant-polymer (ASP) combines both. Polymer and surfactant performance depends on salinity, temperature, adsorption on the rock and injectivity, so candidates are screened in the laboratory and by core flooding before a field pilot.

equipment: polymer or surfactant dissolution and dilution skids

name: CO2 enhanced oil recovery (miscible CO2 flooding)
applications: storage of captured CO2 in oil fields
principle: CO2 is compressed and injected into an oil reservoir, usually one already waterflooded, where at or above the minimum miscibility pressure it mixes with the crude, swells it and lowers its viscosity so that residual oil can be swept to producing wells. Water and CO2 are often injected in alternating slugs (WAG). Produced CO2 is separated from oil and water, recompressed and reinjected, so most purchased CO2 stays underground.

name: Well plug and abandonment (cement plugs, rig-based)
applications: permanent closure of wells at end of life
decommissioning of platforms and subsea wells
principle: A well that is no longer needed is permanently sealed so that formation fluids cannot reach the surface. Barriers, usually cement plugs set across producing zones, above the liner top and near the surface, are placed from a rig after the well is killed and equipment is removed. Standards differ in the barriers they require, for example Indonesia's SNI 13-6910-2002 and Norway's NORSOK D-010, and the choice drives cost. Newer methods such as through-tubing abandonment aim to avoid pulling the completion.
